ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Sick Visit — Jackie Robinson

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for a blister on the right heel

text.paragraph: A blister on the right heel, found last night. [S]

Mr. Robinson asked for a same-day visit. Two days ago he wore new dress shoes for a long day of meetings and a dinner. Last night he found blood on his right sock; he had felt nothing, because his feet are numb, and could not see the heel well, so he used the magnifying mirror and bright lamp he was given and saw a broken blister. He has had no fever, chills, spreading redness or drainage. His glucose readings on the talking meter have run 150 to 210 mg/dL. Separately, he had the regadenoson stress test five days ago; the cardiologist found a small area of reduced blood flow at the bottom of the heart with normal pumping, started metoprolol and nitroglycerin to carry, and chose medical treatment. His chest tightness on stairs has been less since, and he has not needed the nitroglycerin. His vision is a little clearer since the first eye injections. [S]

tr.td: Unroofed blister on the back of the heel, 2.5 by 2 cm, pink moist base, no slough, no surrounding redness, warmth, swelling or odor; does not probe to bone; dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses faint; capillary refill slow

Blurred vision in both eyes, worse over two months, with new floaters in the right eye for four days; acuity by Snellen chart 20/200 right and 20/80 left; undilated view poor on the right; urgent retina examination arranged
S — Synthetic presenting finding, superseded by the retinal diagnosis two days later.
Tightness in the chest on climbing stairs for two months, easing with rest; ECG without acute change; cardiology evaluation with a stress test arranged
S — Synthetic presenting finding, superseded by the coronary diagnosis after the stress test.
Type 2 diabetes for about fifteen years, on metformin and basal insulin, with hyperglycemia (A1c 10.4%)
S — Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented diabetes.
Proliferative diabetic retinopathy in both eyes with center-involving diabetic macular edema (central subfield 412 microns right, 468 left); best-corrected acuity 35 letters right and 56 letters left
S — Synthetic retinal findings anchored to his documented loss of vision.

list.item:
Friction blister of the right heel in a neuropathic foot with peripheral artery disease (S90.821A). Superficial and clean, without infection, so no antibiotic. With loss of sensation and reduced blood flow this is a high-risk wound that needs offloading and close review. [S]
Cleansed and dressed by the clinic nurse; non-adherent dressing changed daily.
Heel offloading shoe; no new shoes until fitted by podiatry.
Visiting nurse three times a week; large-print dressing guide.
Podiatry within two days.
Ankle-brachial index at the four-week visit in nine days.
Return the same day for redness, swelling, drainage, odor or fever.

Coronary artery disease with stable angina (I25.119). Stress imaging with regadenoson, chosen because calf pain limits walking, showed a small reversible inferior defect with an ejection fraction of 56%. Symptoms are mild and improving on metoprolol; medical therapy is appropriate. [S]
Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily and nitroglycerin as needed, as cardiology started.
Continue atorvastatin 80 mg and aspirin.
Call 911 for chest pain that lasts more than five minutes after nitroglycerin.

Type 2 diabetes (E11.65). Readings 150 to 210 mg/dL; no low blood sugar. Healing needs steady glucose, but the gradual plan stands. [S]
Continue the glargine titration plan.

text.paragraph: Follow-up: Visiting nurse from tomorrow; podiatry within two days; review in nine days at the four-week visit with the ankle-brachial index. Next scheduled visit 2026-08-26: four weeks after the new medicines: potassium and creatinine, blood pressure, ankle-brachial index, feet, mood, and the second eye injections. [S]
